name: AKS Secrets and ConfigMap Access
description: Kubernetes Secrets and ConfigMaps hold database passwords, API tokens, and certificates. A principal inside AKS that can read them can walk out with the keys to the rest of the estate. This is not an Azure portal click. It is a kubectl get secret (or equivalent API call) from a pod or a stolen kubeconfig. Broad secret-read from a new service account is credential theft, even if no Azure role changed.
mitigations: Rotate credentials if the actor is compromised
